letters.name: a
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'a' in 'about' or 'sofa'. Keep it short and relaxed — don't stretch it out.

letters.name: ā
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'a' in 'father' — a long, open sound. Hold it twice as long as short 'a'.

letters.name: i
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'i' in 'bit' or 'pin'. Short and crisp — not like 'eye'.

letters.name: ī
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ee' in 'see' or 'bee'. A long, smiling 'i' — hold it for a full beat.

letters.name: u
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'u' in 'put' or 'foot'. Round your lips but keep it short.

letters.name: ū
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'oo' in 'moon' or 'food'. A long rounded 'u' — hold it for a full beat.

letters.name: e
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'e' in 'bet' or 'red'. Short, open 'e' — not drawn out.

letters.name: ē
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ay' in 'say' or 'day' — but without the glide. A pure, long 'e' sound.

letters.name: ai
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'i' in 'like' or 'my'. A diphthong — start with 'a' and glide toward 'i'.

letters.name: o
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'o' in 'hot' or 'not'. Short, open — round your lips briefly.

letters.name: ō
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'o' in 'go' or 'home' — but without the 'w' glide at the end. A pure, long 'o'.

letters.name: au
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ow' in 'now' or 'how'. Start with 'a' and round toward 'u' — a rare but important vowel.

letters.name: ka
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'k' in 'kite'. Between vowels it softens to a 'g'-like sound, but the letter is always 'ka'.

letters.name: ṅa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ng' in 'sing' or 'ring'. This sound never starts a word in Tamil — it appears in the middle or end.

letters.name: ca
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ch' in 'chair' or 'church'. Also pronounced like 's' in some positions — a versatile consonant.

letters.name: ña
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ny' in 'canyon' or Spanish 'ñ' in 'señor'. Rare at word-start — usually found in the middle of words.

letters.name: ṭa
letters.memoryTrick: A retroflex 't' — curl your tongue tip back to touch the roof of your mouth. Harder and deeper than English 't'. Sounds like the 't' in 'stop' said with an Indian accent.

letters.name: ṇa
letters.memoryTrick: A retroflex 'n' — curl your tongue back like for ṭa, but let air flow through your nose. Deeper and heavier than regular 'n'.

letters.name: ta
letters.memoryTrick: A dental 't' — put your tongue tip against the back of your upper teeth. Softer than English 't'. Like the 'th' in 'thin' but without the hiss.

letters.name: na
letters.memoryTrick: A dental 'n' — tongue against the back of your upper teeth, like the 'n' in 'tenth'. Softer than English 'n'.

letters.name: pa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'p' in 'pen' or 'spot'. Between vowels it can soften to a 'b'-like sound, but the letter is always 'pa'.

letters.name: ma
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'm' in 'mother' or 'mango'. Simple and familiar — one of the easiest Tamil letters to remember.

letters.name: ya
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'y' in 'yes' or 'yellow'. A glide consonant — your tongue moves toward the roof of your mouth.

letters.name: ra
letters.memoryTrick: A quick tap of the tongue behind the upper teeth — like the 'tt' in American 'butter' or Spanish 'r' in 'pero'. Not rolled.

letters.name: la
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'l' in 'light' or 'lamp'. A clear, front 'l' — your tongue touches behind your upper teeth.

letters.name: va
letters.memoryTrick: Between English 'v' and 'w' — bring your lips close together without fully touching. Like a soft 'v' or a rounded 'w'.

letters.name: ḻa
letters.memoryTrick: The signature sound of Tamil! Curl your tongue far back in your mouth and let air flow around the sides — a retroflex approximant with no English equivalent. It is the most distinctive sound in the language.

letters.name: ḷa
letters.memoryTrick: A retroflex 'l' — curl your tongue back like for ṭa, but let air flow around the sides. Deeper and heavier than the regular 'la'. Similar to some Swedish or Norwegian retroflex L sounds.

letters.name: ṟa
letters.memoryTrick: A rolled or trilled 'r' — like the Scottish 'r' or Spanish 'rr' in 'perro'. Your tongue tip vibrates against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Stronger than the tapped ra (ர).

letters.name: ṉa
letters.memoryTrick: An alveolar 'n' — your tongue touches the ridge behind your upper teeth, just like English 'n' in 'noon'. One of three 'n' sounds in Tamil — this is the closest to the English one.

letters.name: āytam
letters.memoryTrick: A rare special character — like a light 'h' or the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch'. It appears mostly in classical Tamil and a few modern words. Think of it as a breathy marker.

letters.name: ja
letters.memoryTrick: A Grantha letter used for loanwords. Like 'j' in 'jump' or 'jam'. Borrowed to write Sanskrit and English words in Tamil.

letters.name: ṣa
letters.memoryTrick: A Grantha letter — a retroflex 'sh' sound. Like 'sh' in 'ship' but with your tongue curled back. Used mainly in Sanskrit-derived words.

letters.name: sa
letters.memoryTrick: A Grantha letter for the pure 's' sound. Like 's' in 'sun' or 'see'. Unlike the native ச (which can sound like 'ch'), this is always a clear 's'. Used for Sanskrit and English loanwords.

letters.name: ha
letters.memoryTrick: A Grantha letter — like 'h' in 'hello' or 'house'. Softer and more breathy than a forceful English 'h'. Used in loanwords from Sanskrit and English.

letters.name: ā vowel sign (kombu)
letters.romanization: ā (combines with consonants to form the long 'a' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic mark turns the inherent 'a' of any consonant into a long 'ā'. For example, க (ka) + ா = கா (kā). It is written as a vertical extension on the right side of the consonant.

letters.name: i vowel sign
letters.romanization: i (combines with consonants to form the short 'i' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic changes the vowel to short 'i'. For example, க (ka) + ி = கி (ki). It is written as a hook-like curl above and to the right of the consonant.

letters.name: ī vowel sign
letters.romanization: ī (combines with consonants to form the long 'ī' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic extends the hook further to make the long 'ī'. For example, க (ka) + ீ = கீ (kī). Notice how it is a longer version of the short 'i' sign.

letters.name: u vowel sign
letters.romanization: u (combines with consonants to form the short 'u' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic changes the vowel to short 'u'. For example, க (ka) + ு = கு (ku). It is written as a small curl below and to the right of the consonant.

letters.name: ū vowel sign
letters.romanization: ū (combines with consonants to form the long 'ū' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic makes the long 'ū' — an extended version of the short 'u' sign. For example, க (ka) + ூ = கூ (kū). The extra curl makes it longer.

letters.name: e vowel sign
letters.romanization: e (combines with consonants to form the short 'e' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic changes the vowel to short 'e'. For example, க (ka) + ெ = கெ (ke). Note how this sign goes to the LEFT of the consonant — one of the few signs that precedes the letter it modifies.

letters.name: ē vowel sign
letters.romanization: ē (combines with consonants to form the long 'ē' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic makes the long 'ē'. For example, க (ka) + ே = கே (kē). Like the short 'e' sign, this also goes to the LEFT of the consonant — it looks like a question mark without the dot.

letters.name: ai vowel sign
letters.romanization: ai (combines with consonants to form the 'ai' diphthong)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic creates the 'ai' diphthong. For example, க (ka) + ை = கை (kai). It is a two-part sign — one part goes left of the consonant, the other goes right.

letters.name: o vowel sign
letters.romanization: o (combines with consonants to form the short 'o' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic changes the vowel to short 'o'. For example, க (ka) + ொ = கொ (ko). It is a two-part sign that wraps around the consonant — part goes left, part goes right.

letters.name: ō vowel sign
letters.romanization: ō (combines with consonants to form the long 'ō' vowel)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic makes the long 'ō'. For example, க (ka) + ோ = கோ (kō). Like the short 'o' sign, it wraps around the consonant — the left part is the 'ē' sign and the right part is the 'ā' sign.

letters.name: au vowel sign
letters.romanization: au (combines with consonants to form the 'au' diphthong)
letters.memoryTrick: This diacritic creates the rare 'au' diphthong. For example, க (ka) + ௌ = கௌ (kau). It wraps around the consonant — combining a left-side 'e' sign with a right-side 'au/la' curl.

letters.name: puḷḷi (virama)
letters.romanization: virama — removes the inherent vowel 'a', leaving the bare consonant
letters.ipa: no sound of its own; it suppresses the inherent vowel
letters.memoryTrick: The puḷḷi is a dot placed above a consonant to cancel its built-in 'a' vowel. For example, க = 'ka', but க் = just 'k'. Every consonant carries an invisible 'a' unless the puḷḷi says otherwise.
